facts.timeline_arc: HSBC began [n] emphasizing its India growth engine, highlighted by a booming private‑sector PMI and a lead role in a major SBI capital raise. Mid‑year, the bank was hit by serious regulatory and legal setbacks, including a money‑laundering probe in Switzerland and fines in Hong Kong, while simultaneously pushing into crypto validation and AI initiatives. By the end of [n] and into early [n] HSBC pivoted back to India, championing strong manufacturing data and AI‑driven equity strategies, even as it launched a chief AI officer role amid escalating Middle‑East tensions. The momentum soured in April [n] with a second downgrade of Indian equities and culminated in a surprise $[n] million loss linked to a UK fraud case, underscoring the tension between growth ambitions and emerging risks.

turning_points.why: HSBC faced a major money‑laundering investigation in Switzerland while expanding into decentralized finance as a validator on the Sui blockchain.
The bank reported a profit decline and a large litigation provision, yet highlighted rapid AI expansion, marking a shift toward technology amid financial pressure.
HSBC pivoted its strategy toward India, forecasting strong equity gains as AI‑related trading stalled in other markets.
HSBC created a chief AI officer role, moving from experimental pilots to enterprise‑grade AI, while geopolitical tension in the Middle East disrupted energy routes.
The bank issued a second downgrade on Indian equities, reflecting near‑term market risk despite a bullish macro view anchored in AI and the Asian middle class.
HSBC disclosed a surprise $400 million loss tied to a fraud case in Britain, missing profit estimates and raising concerns over its exposure to private‑credit markets.
